analysis:
Integration of all 17 units. The PR is docs plus one allow-list entry. Changes: a changelog entry; documentation of a Gated DeltaNet four-row prompt-prefill kernel (hardware-support.md, inference.md, cli-reference.md, configuration.md); the literal "DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED" added to LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (LaunchAgent.swift, head ~lines 276-295); and a test (LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift, head 236-258). No change touches the coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody, encryption or prefix-cache storage.

The passthrough remains an explicit allow-list. The test verifies that UNRELATED_SECRET is not forwarded, that the key is not added to WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys (T-043), and that the launchd-resolved mode equals the foreground mode. The variable only selects a kernel: 0/false/no/off keep the stock kernel, packed/rows force a kernel, and anything else probes. It carries no secret or authorization. An operator already controls the provider environment (ADV-001/TB-003), so a forced kernel affecting numerics falls within T-007/T-056, where correct computation is not attested. Forcing a kernel skips the bit-exact probe. That matters only if cached recurrent checkpoints (T-041) are shared across kernels, and the operator already owns local state.

Unverified because the kernel source is outside the supplied evidence: GatedDelta.swift (GatedDeltaPrefill.probe, mode parsing), the bit-exactness claim, and the claimed transient probe memory of about 16 MiB. The claim that qualification environment guards classify the new key was also not confirmed. These are unverified contracts, not regressions. The omitted replay units (38) do not change that. No findings; no threat-model update needed beyond existing coverage. The remaining uncertainty concerns kernel code correctness, not a visible security issue.
